text:
1. The narrative turns away at this point rather than describing what happens.
2. The narrative's silence at this point is itself a form of testimony.
3. Some may object that this silence reflects only the economy of ancient narrative.
4. Ancient narrative rarely reports feelings.
5. Ancient narrative never explains.
6. The objection that the silence is mere narrative economy may be true in some sense.
7. Elsewhere, this narrator does report what characters feel.
8. In this narrative, Esau cries out.
9. In this narrative, Jacob is afraid.
10. In this narrative, Joseph weeps.
11. The narrative's reticence at this point is deliberate.
12. The narrative knows what it is doing.
